intro.title: currentColor and opacity
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple card component with a header and body to learn how to use the `currentColor` keyword and `opacity` property in CSS. You will understand that `currentColor` acts as a dynamic variable that inherits the current text color, allowing for consistent theming, while `opacity` controls the transparency of an element and its children. The main technologies involved are CSS properties for color, borders, and transparency. By the end, you will apply these concepts to style the card's border and background with inherited colors and adjust visibility with opacity, reinforcing how CSS values cascade and interact.
intro.usecase: The currentColor and opacity properties are essential for creating cohesive, maintainable design systems in real-world applications. In dashboard interfaces, currentColor ensures icons and decorative elements automatically match text colors when themes change, while opacity creates subtle hover states on data cards and faded disabled form controls. Product teams use these properties in navigation menus to indicate active states with semi-transparent overlays and in modals to dim background content without hard-coded colors. This approach allows developers to build consistent, theme-aware UIs with minimal CSS maintenance.
